Income Impacts
A comparison of U.S. Census and Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) income data for 1970 show that there was probably from $14.5 to $15.0 million of wage and salary income earned in Big Horn County, of which about $3 million was earned by Indians. In addition, both sources indicate approximately $3 million of non-farm proprietary income and other labor income, of which over 90 percent was received by Anglos. Beyond these estimates of non-agricultural labor income, however, there is no agreement between the two data sources. BEA estimates almost $6 million more income for farm proprietors than does the U.S. Census, and more than $2 million more in transfer payments. Thus, BEA estimates total income for the county in excess of $30 million, while the Census estimate is about $22 million.
Because Westmoreland's activity will have no substantial effect on agricultural proprietary income or on most categories of transfer payments, and because there is obviously a great deal of uncertainty with respect to the value of these flows in 1970, the income analysis that follows is focused on non-agricultural labor income. This is where Westmoreland's impact will be most strongly felt and this is where the data are most reliable.
For details on unemployment rates for various development levels, labor force participation rates and Scenarios see Appendix I, Tables 4 to 20.
